title: Cipla, Teva get USFDA nod for first generic Flovent HFA asthma inhaler
summary: Cipla announced the approval of Fluticasone HFA metered dose inhaler for asthma treatment by the US health regulator. This marks the first generic equivalent to Flovent HFA, expanding treatment options for patients aged four and older. The product was...

contentHtml:
New Delhi, Drug major Cipla on Wednesday said the US health regulator has approved the launch of Fluticasone HFA MDI in 110 mcg and 220 mcg strengths for treatment of asthma.

Fluticasone HFA metered dose inhaler (MDI) is the first generic equivalent to Flovent HFA, Cipla said in a statement.

According to IQVIA, the US market for fluticasone HFA 110 and 220 mcg is approximately USD 350 million, it said.

Jointly developed by Cipla and Teva Pharmaceuticals, the product will be manufactured and supplied by Cipla, while Teva holds the Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA) and will commercialise it in the US.

The inhaled corticosteroid is indicated for the long-term maintenance and prophylactic treatment of asthma in patients aged four years and older, as per the statement.

"This product reinforces our commitment to expanding access to trusted treatment options for patients living with asthma," Cipla MD and Global CEO Achin Gupta said.

Cipla North America CEO Marc Falkin said the opportunity will create meaningful impact and support the company's future US growth journey.
